uncertain.why: Only one fatha is visible over the ت/ب pair, and it sits between the two letters. It is unclear whether ت or ب carries it or whether both do.
The marks over the stacked تج ligature are crowded, so the fatha on ت versus ج cannot be confirmed even at 1400 dpi.
In «إِنَّ لله تِسْعَةً» a low kasra-like stroke appears under the lams of the لله ligature, well below the other marks on the line. It could be a kasra on ل, or a stray mark.

keyA.notes: Page 141 continues the end of prayer 53 from p.140 («مُفَوِّضًا أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ»), so it is marked +. Pages 143 and 144 also continue mid-sentence and are marked +. Every يا before a divine Name has a small fatha at high zoom (it is invisible in the crops), so it is written يَا throughout. Lam-mim words such as الْمَتِينِ, الْمَحْمُودُ, الْمَقَامِ and الْمَوْتَ show the ل sukun stacked over a short fatha stroke; I read the stroke as the fatha on م. Words like آلِهِ, بِهِ, حَوْلِهِ, وَقُوَّتِهِ and مُرَاقَبَتِهِ show only one kasra at the لِه/بِه ligature. I took this as the kasra of the letter and the kasra of ه drawn on top of each other at the same anchor, and wrote both (آلِهِ). Please check this against keyB. The divine Name has a printed case vowel in «إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ» (kasra), «صَلَّى اللَّهُ» and «يَا اللَّهُ» (damma), so the full marks are written there; «حَامِدٍ لله» and «إِنَّ لله» have no case vowel. Quran p.144: the waqf ج printed at the opening bracket of «كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ» (it belongs to «لِلْكُتُبِ ۚ» in the full ayah) is written inside the bracket as «﴿ۚ كَمَا». Prayer numbers are written as printed, with the space after the slash: ٥٩/ ٦٠- and ٦١/ ٦٢-. Commas printed without a following space on p.144 are written with one normal space. The word «استجابَ» on p.144 is printed with a fatha on ب only.

keyB.notes: p141 continues p140 (+); p143 and p144 continue the previous page (+). p144: a waqf sign ۚ (ج) is printed at the opening bracket before «كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ» (Tanzil has it after the preceding word «لِلْكُتُبِ», outside this quotation); kept as ﴿ۚ كَمَا…. p141: no waqf sign printed after «رَمَىٰ» (Tanzil has ۚ). Many words print only one kasra on «آلِه», «حَوْلِه», «وَقُوَّتِه», «مُرَاقَبَتِه», «سُلْطَانِك» (kasra under the letter before final ه/ك only) — transcribed as printed. Stacked mark (sukun over fatha/damma) over lam+next letter read as sukun on lam + vowel on the next letter (e.g. الْمَتِينِ); on p142 first «وَالأَفْعَالِ» the lam has no separate sukun (the stack sits on the hamza: fatha + sukun of ف), unlike the later «وَالْأَفْعَالِ». «وبَارِكْ» printed without fatha on و except in no.63 (وَبَارِكْ). «استجابَ» (p144) printed without harakat except final fatha.
